ON NON-FIRM RISK

The Non-Firm Power Risk Index

Princeps Research · June 2026

INTRODUCTION

The connections clearing fastest are non-firm — interruptible by contract. The market prices damage; the peril is availability.

Britain is reconnecting industry to a network that cannot promise firm power at queue speed. Data centres and grid-scale assets contract for always-on availability while the connections that clear retain the operator's right to curtail under Gate 1 terms.1,2 That gap — between what the asset loses and what the policy pays — is the subject of this index.3,4

Reindustrialisation and compute build-out are not waiting for firm connections. Demand-side reform is consulting on the right to curtail very large users; the queue already runs to triple-digit gigawatts.5 The peril is no longer a tail event in a hazard module — it is a register fact on the connection agreement.

We scored 115 UK insurance-market participants — 39 carriers, 35 MGAs and brokers, 24 assets, 17 reinsurers — on Exposure to non-firm load and Preparedness to underwrite it, then reduced each to a single number: Margin of Safety = Preparedness − Exposure.

EXPOSURE

How large is the bet? Exposure asks how much of the book, portfolio, or asset base sits on interruptible connections — and how correlated that concentration is when a constraint event bites more than one insured at once.6,7

Five sub-factors carry the score: book concentration on energy and compute, non-firm intensity (from TEC gate status and embedded-capacity registers where measured), aggregation on shared grid geography, the trigger gap between damage-BI wordings and curtailment loss, and tenor mismatch between multi-year cover and a peril with almost no claims history.

EXPOSURE

book concentrationw 0.30

How concentrated is the entity's relevant book in UK power / energy / data-centre infrastructure?

non firm intensityw 0.25

What share of the insured/owned assets sit on non-firm, flexible or interruptible grid connections?

non firm compute exposurew 0.25

How severe is the multiplicative coupling of compute load, non-firm connection, and boundary curtailment likelihood?

aggregation correlationw 0.20

How vulnerable is the entity to a single grid / curtailment event hitting many insureds at once?

trigger gapw 0.15

How reliant is the entity on legacy physical-damage triggers against losses that are contractual / SLA / non-damage in nature?

tenor mismatchw 0.10

How much long-dated cover is written against a thin / short claims history?

PREPAREDNESS

Can this entity actually carry the risk it has written? Preparedness is not capital alone — it is whether the form, the data, and the pricing model see curtailment as a first-class peril rather than a property-damage footnote.8,9

Product fit is the hinge: parametric availability triggers, SLA mirrors, and curtailment indices exist in fragments; most carrier wordings still wait for physical damage. Underwriting expertise, telemetry, reinsurance depth, and pricing models must span power and interruption — not cat hazard footprints.10,11

PREPAREDNESS

data monitoringw 0.25

Does the entity have availability / curtailment telemetry and loss data that lets the risk be priced?

product fitw 0.20

Does the entity use parametric / availability-trigger / non-damage BI structures vs off-the-shelf property/BI?

underwriting expertisew 0.20

Does the entity have specialist energy-plus-technology talent able to span power and cyber/tech lines?

capital reinsurancew 0.20

How deep and stable is the capacity / reinsurance behind this line; can it absorb a correlated event?

pricing modellingw 0.15

How sophisticated is the entity at modelling curtailment probability, correlation and connection-status risk?

THE FOUR QUADRANTS

115 entities on the current slice, split at the in-sample median (exposure ≥ 56.2, preparedness ≥ 61.2). Dot size = confidence; inner fill = measured share. Roughly 26% sit Exposed — high bet, weak means — and 25% in Whitespace, where rated paper could deploy if the trigger gap closes.

MARGIN OF SAFETY VS MEASURED SHARE

A large positive margin on assessed inputs alone is a hypothesis, not a finding. The scatter below plots Margin of Safety against each entity's measured/disclosed share — the epistemic hygiene the L5 publication gate enforces. At 16% blended measured share the index remains PROVISIONAL; regression slope will move as register tiers land.

MARGIN OF SAFETY BY LAYER

The stack carries different parts of the same correlated cluster. Carriers (L1) average a modest positive margin; underlying assets (L3) show the deepest negative spreads — exposure on Gate-1 connections runs ahead of any single carrier's preparedness score.39 carriers · 35 market participants · 24 assets · 17 reinsurers.

Heaviest exposed concentration sits in Layer 3 (assets) (19 of 30). Whitespace carriers named in the current slice include Beazley, SCOR Syndicate 2015 (formerly The Channel Syndicate), Chaucer / Lloyd's Syndicate 1084, Atrium Underwriters / Lloyd's Syndicate 609 and 6 others — the placement question is not whether capacity exists, but whether wordings match the peril.

MARGIN OF SAFETY BY BOOK SEGMENT

Segment tags (energy, data centre, parametric MGA, broker, reinsurance) expose where the margin compresses — data-centre and energy assets carry the most negative means; parametric and broker layers sit closer to neutral because product design already chases non-damage triggers.

CARRIER-LEVEL DATA

At carrier level, exposure and preparedness diverge in ways the headline score hides. A syndicate with strong capital and weak register measurement can sit in whitespace on assessed inputs alone — until Gate 2 status lands on a linked asset and the deterministic tier moves.

Cat models are the wrong architecture: there is no licensable hazard module for lawful switch-off. The correlated loss is geographic and contractual — shared constraint boundaries and damage-only triggers — not a seismic zone or wind footprint.3,4

THE DIVERSIFIED CARRIER'S PROBLEM

Select a carrier: each dot is one underlying asset positioned by its Margin of Safety; the dashed line is the carrier average. A diversified renewable or DC book can look adequate at the syndicate level while linked assets cluster exposed — aggregation the headline MoS does not show.

THE TRIGGER GAP

The market's conventional answer — property damage plus business interruption — fires on breakage. Curtailment loss is contractual: the operator exercises a lawful right to interrupt, the asset breaches an SLA, and revenue stops with the plant intact.4,11

Basis risk is not a modelling refinement — it is the gap between the peril and the trigger. Until availability is indexed to register-native measurement, every curtailment hour is an unfunded loss.

HOW IT OPERATES AT EVERY LEVEL

L3
Energy & data-centre assets — the insured exposure
Where the peril sits: a non-firm, curtailable connection on a constrained boundary. The cover attaches here as parametric availability cover, the trigger calibrated to the asset's boundary curtailment probability and connection-gate status.
Inputs: NESO TEC gate status, DNO flexible-connection share, boundary congestion. Cover: hours-of-availability index, indemnity per curtailed hour.
L2
MGAs & brokers — structure and placement
Translate exposure into a placeable contract: set the parametric index, attachment and limit, and place the gap damage-based wordings leave open. NFRI is the underwriting file that justifies the rate to capacity.
Uses: Margin-of-Safety rank, sub-factor decomposition, evidence tiers per rating.
L1
Carriers & Lloyd's syndicates — carry the risk
Hold the cover on balance sheet. NFRI flags where a book's exposure has run ahead of its preparedness — the negative Margin of Safety that surfaces accumulating risk before the loss history arrives.
Uses: portfolio Margin-of-Safety distribution, book concentration, capital/reinsurance adequacy.
L4
Reinsurers & capacity — aggregate and cede
Stand behind the tower. The decisive question is correlation: how much non-firm exposure shares the same grid geography and curtails together. NFRI's aggregation factor prices that shared-boundary accumulation directly.
Uses: aggregation-correlation over constraint boundaries, HHI on shared geography.

ON TRANSFORMATION

The index is not the product. It is the wedge: register-native measurement of a peril the market underwrites blind — so the cover that closes the trigger gap can be priced, reinsured, and placed with eyes open.2,18

Parametric availability, SLA mirrors, curtailment indices — the fragments exist. No one yet holds the full stack: measured non-firm exposure, basis-minimised trigger, aggregation-aware pricing, and rated paper in whitespace.

Five levers reindustrialisation cannot skip

01
Connection reform

Firmness becomes a register fact — Gate 1/2 is the measurement substrate.

02
Affordable electrons

Flexible queue clearance trades curtailment for speed; the cost is already in constraint data.

03
Availability cover

Parametric and SLA wordings close the trigger gap damage-BI leaves open.

04
Aggregation visibility

Grid geography correlates risk; dependency models do not see it.

05
Builder capital

Whitespace carriers with rated paper are where unwritten cover should start.

Brokers and MGAs have already placed parametric and SLA structures around DC and renewable risk — the line forming around the gap, not yet a full carrier stack.10,9

WHY NOW

Gate 1 and Gate 2 made firmness a register fact — not a negotiating point.1 CMP448 priced progression into the Gate-2 queue from January 2026.13 Demand-side reform is consulting on curtailment rights for the largest users. The rules landed before the market repriced who can carry the interruptible half.

Brokers have placed billion-dollar DC facilities on non-firm terms; the constraint cost curve is observable in NESO data while BI rates on damage triggers stay flat. That combination — rising physical cost, flat premium on the wrong peril — is the definition of mispricing.

Publication gate — eval before publish. Current slice: 16% measured.
